# Call onError for a rejection that is not an Error

Issue: re-cinq/HALEngine#95
Labels: priority:medium, type:bug, size:S, area:api

## Why

The orchestrator's `catch` gates `onError` on `error instanceof Error`. A rejection that is not an `Error` — a thrown string, a plain object, a value from a library that rejects with its own shape — bypasses `onError` entirely while still propagating to the caller.

`onError` is the seam a deployer uses to count failures, page someone, or write an incident record. A gate that silently drops a class of failures makes it a liar in exactly the cases nobody tested for, and the deployer's dashboard reads "no errors" while the caller sees rejections.

Recorded as measured behaviour in `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` by HALEngine#83, which scoped itself to specifying the seam rather than changing it, and raised again by the reviewer on that PR. The spec notes this property is owned by no issue in the epic; this is that issue.

## What to do

Call `onError` for every rejection. Whatever is not already an `Error` gets wrapped in one, preserving the original as the `cause`, so a hook typed against `Error` keeps compiling and a hook that wants the raw value can still reach it. The re-thrown value at the caller boundary stays exactly what it is today, so nothing downstream changes shape.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A provider rejecting with a string calls `onError` once, with an `Error` whose `cause` is that string, and the caller still receives the original rejection unchanged
- [ ] The same holds for a rejection with a plain object and with `undefined`
- [ ] A rejection that is already an `Error` reaches `onError` as the same instance, not a wrapper, pinned by the existing tests remaining unedited
- [ ] `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` replaces its recorded-flaw line with the new guarantee, and the CHANGELOG says what changes for an existing consumer
- [ ] `npm run build`, `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run eslint` (`--max-warnings 0`) and `npm run prettier:check` pass

## Tech notes

Key files: `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` (the `catch` and its `instanceof Error` gate), `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md`.

Out of scope: `beforeSession` escaping the `try` (its own issue) and usage accounting across tool rounds (HALEngine#93).

# Definition of Done

> The orchestrator's `catch` gates `onError` on `error instanceof Error`. A rejection that is not an `Error` — a thrown string, a plain object, a response body rejected directly by an HTTP client — bypasses `onError` entirely while still propagating to the caller.

**Strategy: `direct`** — the seam already exists. `createChatOrchestrator` returns an orchestrator whose `processMessage` and `processMessageStream` invoke the installed `OrchestratorHooks`. A test can drive `processMessage` with a provider that throws a string or a plain object and observe that `onError` is bypassed today because of the `error instanceof Error` gate in the `catch` block.

## Done when these pass

- [ ] **calls onError with an Error carrying the thrown string and runs afterSession while rethrowing** — when a turn rejects with a string (`'string boom'`), `onError` is called once with an `Error` instance whose `message` is `'string boom'`, `afterSession` runs after `onError`, and the rejection still propagates to the caller. Fails today because `onError` is skipped (`callOrder` is `['afterSession']` and `isError` is `false`).
      `src/orchestration/onErrorNonError.acceptance.test.ts`

- [ ] **calls onError with an Error carrying a readable message when the stream rejects with a plain object** — when a turn rejects with a plain object (`{code: 503, detail: 'upstream down'}`), `onError` is called once with an `Error` instance carrying a non-empty `message`, `afterSession` runs after `onError`, and the rejection still propagates to the caller. Fails today because `onError` is skipped (`callOrder` is `['afterSession']` and `isError` is `false`).
      `src/orchestration/onErrorNonError.acceptance.test.ts`

## Facets

- [x] In `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts`, coerce a caught non-`Error` rejection to an `Error` with a readable `message` (while passing an `Error` instance through unchanged) so `hooks.onError` always fires on any rejection inside the `try` block.
- [ ] Confirm existing `Error`-instance tests in `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts` (`called with session and error when stream fails`, `error still propagates after onError hook`, `error path calls onError then afterSession`) remain green without modification.
- [x] Add a `CHANGELOG.md` entry under `## [Unreleased]` describing the behaviour change for existing consumers.

- [x] Expose the stamped spec anchor in the new test descriptor: `scripts/lore-list-tests.mjs` currently emits no `spec` field.

- [ ] Associate individual tests with their own anchors when a test file contains multiple spec stamps.

## Out of scope

- `beforeSession` escaping the `try` block (resolved separately in HALEngine#94).
- Usage accounting across tool rounds (resolved separately in HALEngine#93).
- Widening the `onError` hook parameter type away from `Error` (the ticket keeps `(session: ChatSession, error: Error) => Promise<void>`).

<document source="specs/hal-engine-spec-anchor-drift/spec.md" type="spec" relevance="1.00" tokens="1286">
## Rotten anchors

Independent of any baseline, an anchor must land somewhere real. Four ways it does not, all reported as `rotten` and all failing the run in both modes:

- the cited file does not exist in the working tree ([validated by: reports a citation into a file that is not in the working tree @dc5ecb39](../../scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.test.ts#L291)).
- the line is past the end of the file ([validated by: reports an anchor past the end of the cited file @c6efe207](../../scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.test.ts#L299)).
- the line is blank, or holds only closing punctuation — `)`, `]`, `}`, `>`, `,`, `;` ([validated by: fails in both modes when the anchor lands on a blank line @c5012021](../../scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.test.ts#L263), [closing punctuation @09920dc2](../../scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.test.ts#L279)).
- the line is in a test file but is not the `it`/`test`/`describe` declaration ([validated by: reports an anchor that lands inside the test body as rotten @11be2126](../../scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.test.ts#L551)).

A rotten href is reported rather than quietly synced: a short-form label whose href lands on a blank line leaves both modes failing with nothing rewritten, instead of the label being pulled into agreement with a broken target ([validated by: reports a label whose href is rotten rather than silently syncing it @dbce21d7](../../scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.test.ts#L435)).

The last two are the ones that matter in practice. A citation that slides onto the closing bracket of the block it meant to name still resolves and still renders; it just proves nothing. A citation that slides onto an `expect` inside the body is worse, because it reads as a precise reference to a line no reader can turn back into the name of a case.

The declaration check is narrow on purpose:

- The declaration itself passes, and so does the enclosing `describe` — citing a group is a legitimate reference ([validated by: accepts an anchor on the it declaration itself @cb5b28cc](../../scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.test.ts#L533), [describe@5489d08c](../../scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.test.ts#L542)).
- Modified forms are declarations too: `it.each`, `test.skip` and the `f`/`x` prefixes all pass ([validated by: accepts the modified forms of a declaration @22f7d888](../../scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.test.ts#L573)).
- Only test files are held to it. A citation into a workflow, a config or `package.json` has no declaration to land on and is exempt ([validated by: holds only test files to the rule, so a non-declaration line elsewhere passes @136b90f5](../../scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.test.ts#L600)).
- It fails the plain run as well as `--check`, and rewrites nothing ([validated by: fails a body-line anchor in rewrite mode too, and rewrites nothing @910a3d66](../../scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.test.ts#L560)).
- It composes with repointing rather than replacing it: a test citation still moves from one declaration to another as lines shift above it ([validated by: repoints a test citation from one declaration to another as lines shift @14cbf42d](../../scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.test.ts#L583)).

What it does not catch is a citation aimed at the wrong declaration. `#Lnn` on a real but unintended `it` passes every check here, because nothing mechanical relates a statement's prose to a test's name. That failure mode is a review concern, and the `require-spec-link` backlog is the instrument that surfaces it: the test the citation should have named goes on reading as uncited.

## What counts as an anchor

Any relative path with a file extension followed by `#L<n>`, in any spec under `specs/<slug>/spec.md` plus `.specify/spec.md`. A link whose fragment is not a line number is not an anchor and is left alone, however much the file around it moves ([validated by: leaves a link whose fragment is not a line number untouched @a947cfb5](../../scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.test.ts#L506)). Test files are the common case, but nothing restricts it to them: a citation into a workflow, a config or a script is repointed the same way ([validated by: repoints docs, README and script citations alike @127cbc78](../../scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.test.ts#L454), [root config @530a00d8](../../scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.test.ts#L476), [workflow and manifest @5ac541e6](../../scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.test.ts#L490)).

The label is not part of the anchor. A descriptive label such as `[validated by]` is never touched ([validated by: leaves a descriptive label alone while syncing a short-form one beside it @034187d7](../../scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.test.ts#L420)). A short-form `[Lnn](../../src/X.test.ts#Lnn)` is different: its label carries no meaning beyond the number, so it is force-synced to whatever its own href says ([validated by: syncs labels even in a spec skipped for a differing anchor set @5c7bbfe3](../../scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.test.ts#L399)). Syncing happens after the rewrite, so a repointed href carries its label with it in the same run ([validated by: carries the label along when the href is repointed @fb6530ce](../../scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.test.ts#L354)).
</document>
<document source="AGENTS.md" type="doc" relevance="0.51" tokens="987">
## Spec Test Links

Statements in `specs/*/spec.md` cite their validating test in a trailing
parenthetical at the end of the statement, where a list item counts as one
statement and a paragraph counts per sentence. Tests live beside their source
in this repo, so the path points into `src/`:

```markdown
- All entries within a single assistant response are committed before the next
  user message is processed
  ([validated by: commits every entry before the next user message](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L42)).
```

The citation carries the test's **name** as well as its line. The name is what the
author cited; the line is a derived pointer, and it goes stale on its own - adding
an import above a suite moves every test below it, and the citation lands on a
different, still-valid declaration without anything noticing. `npm run spec:names`
holds each citation to the test it names, and `npm run spec:names:fix` repoints the
line from the name. The `#Lnn` stays because the lint rule and the coverage job
both index by it; a citation without one marks the whole file covered rather than
one test.

A citation counts as coverage only where it is trailing, and a test link placed
anywhere else in the statement is a misplaced citation rather than a weaker one.
Upstream `check:spec-links` reports it and exits 1, and the coverage job that
consumes these specs records nothing for it - so a spec can read as fully cited while its coverage is
zero. A mid-statement link to something that is not a test file - a script, a
doc, another spec - is ordinary prose, is never reported, and was never coverage
to begin with. A misplaced citation is fixed by moving it to the end of its
statement, never by deleting it.

In a test file the `#Lnn` anchor must land on the `it(`, `test(` or `describe(`
declaration itself - not a blank line, not one holding only closing punctuation,
and not a line inside the test body. A citation onto an `expect` renders and
resolves like any other, and proves nothing: no reader can turn that line back
into the name of a case. `scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.mjs` reports all four as
`rotten` and exits 1 in both modes. A citation into a file that is not a test -
a workflow, a config, `package.json` - has no declaration to land on and is held
only to existing and carrying content.

What no gate can catch is an anchor aimed at the wrong declaration: a real but
unintended `it(` passes every check. The tell is that the test the statement
meant to cite goes on reading as uncited in the `require-spec-link` backlog.

Anchors drift silently whenever a cited file gains or loses lines above them, so
after editing any cited file re-run `node scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.mjs`
rather than hand-correcting the numbers. That script cannot repair a spec absent
from the base ref, since it has no baseline to translate from; on the branch that
introduces a spec, its anchors have to be corrected by hand.

The convention's tooling is wired up here: `npm run check:spec-links`, `npm run check:spec-status` and
`node scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.mjs --check origin/main` all gate CI, and
`re-lint/require-status-matches-coverage` derives each `Status` row from its
spec's citations - from the ones that are evidence, since 1.8.0 of the plugin: a citation
whose file is gone, or whose `#Lnn` lands outside any `it()`/`test()` declaration, counts
for nothing, so a drifted anchor costs a spec its tier rather than quietly holding it. That
rule now also carries a fixer that rewrites the `Status` row, so `eslint --fix` run over the
tree will restate a spec's status for you; no CI job here runs one.
`re-lint/require-spec-link` gates in `eslint.config.mjs`: every test cites a
statement, so an uncited new test fails the build. Its statement-side mirror,
`require-statement-links`, runs at `warn` from `eslint.config.backlog.mjs` and
reports without blocking - the severities the rule pair is designed for.
</document>
